title: Industrial radiography operations, monitoring, surveys and posting practice questions
description: Practice questions on NRC 10 CFR Part 34: operating procedures, dosimeters, alarm ratemeters, surveys, surveillance, posting and records.

questions.question: Under 34.41(c), a licensee may conduct lay-barge, offshore platform, or underwater radiography only if what condition is met?

options.A: The radiography is performed inside a permanent radiographic installation
options.B: Procedures have been approved by the Commission or by an Agreement State
options.C: The Radiation Safety Officer is personally present on the barge or platform
options.D: Each exposure is limited to one sealed source per workday

questions.explanation: 34.41(c) says a licensee may conduct this work "only if procedures have been approved by the Commission or by an Agreement State."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.41, Conducting industrial radiographic operations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: A licensee may conduct lay-barge, offshore platform, or underwater radiography only if procedures have been approved by the Commission or by an Agreement State.

questions.question: At a temporary job site, who does 34.51 name as the person who shall maintain continuous direct visual surveillance of the radiographic operation?

options.A: The Radiation Safety Officer only
options.B: A security guard posted at each entrance to the area
options.C: The licensee's site manager or client representative
options.D: The radiographer, or the other individual present, as required by 34.41

questions.explanation: 34.51 says "the radiographer, or the other individual present, as required by § 34.41, shall maintain continuous direct visual surveillance of the operation".

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.51, Surveillance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: During each radiographic operation the radiographer, or the other individual present, as required by § 34.41, shall maintain continuous direct visual surveillance of the operation

questions.question: 34.51 makes an exception to the continuous direct visual surveillance requirement for which locations?

options.A: Permanent radiographic installations where all entryways are locked and the requirements of 34.33 are met
options.B: Temporary job sites where the area boundary has been roped off and posted
options.C: Field stations where two qualified individuals are present
options.D: Any location where the operation lasts less than one hour

questions.explanation: The surveillance duty applies "except at permanent radiographic installations where all entryways are locked and the requirements of § 34.33 are met."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.51, Surveillance (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: except at permanent radiographic installations where all entryways are locked and the requirements of § 34.33 are met.

questions.question: What does 34.53 say about the posting exceptions listed in 10 CFR 20.1903?

options.A: They apply only at permanent radiographic installations
options.B: They apply when the area is under continuous direct visual surveillance
options.C: They do not apply to industrial radiographic operations
options.D: They apply if the Radiation Safety Officer approves them in writing

questions.explanation: 34.53 says "Exceptions listed in § 20.1903 of this chapter do not apply to industrial radiographic operations."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.53, Posting (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Exceptions listed in § 20.1903 of this chapter do not apply to industrial radiographic operations.

questions.question: Under 34.45(a)(12), when must operating and emergency procedures include a source recovery procedure?

options.A: If the licensee will perform source recovery
options.B: Only when radiography is performed underwater
options.C: Only at permanent radiographic installations
options.D: Whenever the licensee employs radiographers' assistants

questions.explanation: 34.45(a)(12) lists a "Source recovery procedure if licensee will perform source recovery".

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.45, Operating and emergency procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Source recovery procedure if licensee will perform source recovery;

questions.question: A radiographer's alarm ratemeter alarms unexpectedly at a job site. Under 34.45(a)(8), what must the operating and emergency procedures contain for this event?

options.A: A form the RSO must sign within 30 days
options.B: The name of the company that calibrates the ratemeter
options.C: Steps that must be taken immediately by radiography personnel
options.D: A schedule for replacing the ratemeter's battery

questions.explanation: The procedures must include "Steps that must be taken immediately by radiography personnel in the event a pocket dosimeter is found to be off-scale or an alarm ratemeter alarms unexpectedly."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.45, Operating and emergency procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Steps that must be taken immediately by radiography personnel in the event a pocket dosimeter is found to be off-scale or an alarm ratemeter alarms unexpectedly.

questions.question: Which two accident-related instructions does 34.45(a) require in operating and emergency procedures?

options.A: Estimating property damage and filing an insurance claim
options.B: Preparing a press release and notifying nearby residents
options.C: Disciplining the personnel involved and retraining them
options.D: Notifying proper persons and minimizing exposure of persons in the event of an accident

questions.explanation: 34.45(a) lists "The procedure for notifying proper persons in the event of an accident" and "Minimizing exposure of persons in the event of an accident".

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.45, Operating and emergency procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: (10) The procedure for notifying proper persons in the event of an accident; (11) Minimizing exposure of persons in the event of an accident;

questions.question: Under 34.47(a), where must a radiographer wear the direct reading dosimeter, alarm ratemeter and personnel dosimeter?

options.A: On the wrist of the hand nearest the source
options.B: On the trunk of the body
options.C: On the outside of the collar
options.D: Anywhere within the individual's reach

questions.explanation: Each individual must wear these items "on the trunk of the body" at all times during radiographic operations.

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.47, Personnel monitoring (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: each individual wears, on the trunk of the body, a direct reading dosimeter, an operating alarm ratemeter, and a personnel dosimeter.

questions.question: 34.47(a) lists three items each radiographer wears during radiographic operations. At a permanent radiography installation where other appropriate alarming or warning devices are in routine use, which item does the rule say the radiographer is exempt from wearing?

options.A: A direct reading dosimeter
options.B: A personnel dosimeter
options.C: None of the three; the rule gives no exemption at any installation
options.D: An alarming ratemeter

questions.explanation: 34.47(a) says that at such installations "the wearing of an alarming ratemeter is not required."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.47, Personnel monitoring (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: At permanent radiography installations where other appropriate alarming or warning devices are in routine use, the wearing of an alarming ratemeter is not required.

questions.question: Under 34.47(a)(1), electronic personal dosimeters may only be used in place of what?

options.A: Ion-chamber pocket dosimeters
options.B: Alarm ratemeters
options.C: Film badges
options.D: Radiation survey instruments

questions.explanation: 34.47(a)(1) says "Electronic personal dosimeters may only be used in place of ion-chamber pocket dosimeters."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.47, Personnel monitoring (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Electronic personal dosimeters may only be used in place of ion-chamber pocket dosimeters.

questions.question: 34.47(a)(3) says all personnel dosimeters must be evaluated at least quarterly or promptly after replacement. Which of the two applies?

options.A: Whichever is less frequent
options.B: Whichever the radiographer chooses
options.C: Whichever is more frequent
options.D: Quarterly only, unless the dosimeter is a film badge

questions.explanation: Personnel dosimeters must be evaluated "at least quarterly or promptly after replacement, whichever is more frequent."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.47, Personnel monitoring (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: All personnel dosimeters must be evaluated at least quarterly or promptly after replacement, whichever is more frequent.

questions.question: Under 34.47(b), when must direct reading dosimeters be read and the exposures recorded?

options.A: At the end of each work week
options.B: At the beginning and end of each shift
options.C: Once for each job site
options.D: Only when the dosimeter reads above its midpoint

questions.explanation: Direct reading dosimeters "must be read and the exposures recorded at the beginning and end of each shift".

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.47, Personnel monitoring (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: must be read and the exposures recorded at the beginning and end of each shift

questions.question: A radiographer's pocket chamber is found off-scale and radiation exposure cannot be ruled out as the cause. What time period does 34.47(d) set for sending the personnel dosimeter that requires processing for processing and evaluation?

options.A: Within 24 hours
options.B: Within 30 days
options.C: By the end of the calendar quarter
options.D: Within 6 months

questions.explanation: The personnel dosimeter that requires processing "must be sent for processing and evaluation within 24 hours."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.47, Personnel monitoring (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: the individual's personnel dosimeter that requires processing must be sent for processing and evaluation within 24 hours.

questions.question: A radiographer's electronic personal dosimeter reads greater than 2 millisieverts (200 millirems), and exposure cannot be ruled out. Under 34.47(d), who must make the determination of the individual's radiation dose before the individual resumes work?

options.A: The radiographer trainer
options.B: The dosimetry processor
options.C: The individual's co-worker radiographer
options.D: The RSO or the RSO's designee

questions.explanation: The individual may not resume work until a dose determination is made, and "This determination must be made by the RSO or the RSO's designee."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.47, Personnel monitoring (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: This determination must be made by the RSO or the RSO's designee.

questions.question: A radiographer's assistant finds that the personnel dosimeter required by 34.47(a) has been lost. What does 34.47(e) require of the worker?

options.A: Borrow a co-worker's personnel dosimeter and continue working
options.B: Cease work immediately until a replacement is provided and the exposure is calculated
options.C: Finish the shift and report the loss at the next quarterly evaluation
options.D: Continue working as long as the alarm ratemeter is operating

questions.explanation: The worker "shall cease work immediately until a replacement personnel dosimeter meeting the requirements in paragraph (a) is provided and the exposure is calculated".

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.47, Personnel monitoring (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: the worker shall cease work immediately until a replacement personnel dosimeter meeting the requirements in paragraph (a) is provided and the exposure is calculated

questions.question: Under 34.47(g)(2), at what preset dose rate must each alarm ratemeter be set to give an alarm signal?

options.A: 0.5 mSv/hr (50 mrem/hr)
options.B: 20 mSv/hr (2,000 mrem/hr)
options.C: 5 mSv/hr (500 mrem/hr)
options.D: 50 mSv/hr (5,000 mrem/hr)

questions.explanation: Each alarm ratemeter must "Be set to give an alarm signal at a preset dose rate of 5 mSv/hr (500 mrem/hr)".

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.47, Personnel monitoring (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Be set to give an alarm signal at a preset dose rate of 5 mSv/hr (500 mrem/hr);

questions.question: Under 34.49(b), the survey after each exposure must determine that the sealed source has returned to its shielded position before which actions?

options.A: Exchanging films, repositioning the exposure head, or dismantling equipment
options.B: Writing the utilization log entry for the day
options.C: Reading the direct reading dosimeters at the end of the shift
options.D: Recharging the pocket dosimeters for the next shift

questions.explanation: The survey "must determine that the sealed source has returned to its shielded position before exchanging films, repositioning the exposure head, or dismantling equipment."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.49, Radiation surveys (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The survey must determine that the sealed source has returned to its shielded position before exchanging films, repositioning the exposure head, or dismantling equipment.

questions.question: Besides the survey after each exposure, when does 34.49(c) require a survey of the radiographic exposure device with a calibrated radiation survey instrument?

options.A: Only at the start of each calendar quarter
options.B: Only when a new radiographer's assistant is assigned to the crew
options.C: Only after the device has been transported on a public road
options.D: Any time the source is exchanged and whenever the device is placed in a storage area

questions.explanation: 34.49(c) requires a survey "any time the source is exchanged and whenever a radiographic exposure device is placed in a storage area (as defined in § 34.3), to ensure that the sealed source is in its shielded position."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.49, Radiation surveys (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: any time the source is exchanged and whenever a radiographic exposure device is placed in a storage area (as defined in § 34.3), to ensure that the sealed source is in its shielded position.

questions.topic: Records of procedures, monitoring and surveys
questions.question: What retention period does 34.83(c) set for personnel dosimeter results?

options.A: For 3 years after the record is made
options.B: For 1 year after the individual stops working for the licensee
options.C: Until the Commission terminates the license
options.D: Until the next quarterly evaluation

questions.explanation: 34.83(c) lists "Personnel dosimeter results until the Commission terminates the license."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.83, Records of personnel monitoring procedures (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Personnel dosimeter results until the Commission terminates the license.

questions.topic: Records of procedures, monitoring and surveys
questions.question: Under 34.85, which exposure device survey must the licensee keep a record of?

options.A: Only the first survey performed in each workday
options.B: The survey before the device is placed in storage under 34.49(c), if it is the last one performed in the workday
options.C: Only surveys performed at temporary job sites
options.D: Only surveys performed by the Radiation Safety Officer

questions.explanation: 34.85 requires "a record of each exposure device survey conducted before the device is placed in storage as specified in § 34.49(c), if that survey is the last one performed in the workday."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.85, Records of radiation surveys (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Each licensee shall maintain a record of each exposure device survey conducted before the device is placed in storage as specified in § 34.49(c), if that survey is the last one performed in the workday.
